subject: Geo-binding playbook & log retention scope — HealthCore discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@healthcore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: geo-binding constraints + logging questions (HealthCore)

Janet — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the items we need to confirm to progress the PoC/contract: 

Key points from the call
- Primary requirement: processing for US patient/claims data must remain in US data centers by default.
- Secondary: for certain EU-originated records (consented subset) you may want EU residency and longer logs.
- PII policy: HealthCore requires token-level pseudonymization at rest plus ability to delete raw inputs on demand.
- Logging: security/ops want audit logs (auth, request metadata) retained for 12 months; application-level logs can be shorter.

Open asks (please confirm):
1) For the EU subset, does HealthCore require strict geo-locking (no cross-region backup), or is warm-standby acceptable (replicated encrypted backups in EU with failover manual/controlled)?
2) For US data, is cross-region failover to another US region acceptable for DR, or do you require single-region restore-only?
3) Confirm retention: PII deletions after 90 days vs 30 days? You mentioned 90 in passing but want explicit confirmation.
4) Which artifact(s) should we include in the SOC2 packet? I attached the evidence request template; please flag priority items.

Next steps we propose
- Technical workshop (1 hour) to map actual routing: pinning vs warm-standby and encryption key scope (KMS/HSM). Karthik can run it.
- We’ll prepare two playbook options: (A) strict geo-lock (EU-only backups) and (B) warm-standby (encrypted EU backups + manual failover).
- Deliver preliminary costs/latency delta for both options.

If you can confirm the answers to the open asks above by EOD Mon, Nov 30, we’ll send the playbook drafts and a calendar invite for the workshop next week.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call: geo-binding constraints + logging questions (HealthCore)

Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side below (high level; I've included Markus for technical confirmation):

Answers to your open asks
1) EU subset: strict geo-locking preferred for PHI-derived EU records. We cannot allow replicas of that subset to leave EU boundaries without explicit patient-level consent; backups must remain in EU.
2) US data failover: cross-region within US is acceptable for DR; prefer automatic failover only between us-west and us-east pools, not to EU.
3) Retention: PII (raw inputs) — 90 days default; security logs/audit trail — 12 months. Application-level logs — 180 days.
4) SOC2 packet: please include network diagrams, KMS/HSM key handling procedures, and a sample audit log export. I attached the SOC2 evidence request from our compliance team (stub).

Additional notes
- We require a delete-on-request API that can remove customer-level raw inputs and any cached prefixes within 48 hours of request.
- For EU geo-locking, we need export/import proofs for backups (manifest with region ids) and quarterly attestations while under contract.

Markus — can you confirm the technical feasibility of (a) per-customer region pinning for the EU subset and (b) whether snapshot backups can be retained in EU-only storage with manual cross-checks?

Thanks,
Janet
Director, Product Security — HealthCore
janet.lowe@healthcore.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: geo-binding constraints + logging questions (HealthCore)

Janet / Markus — thanks, this is helpful. Quick technical notes from our side and feasibility summary: 

Feasibility summary
- Per-customer region pinning: feasible. We can pin a tenant to a region at the account level; pinned tenants use local storage and local inference pools.
- EU-only backups for pinned tenants: feasible if you select our EU private/storage option and we scope KMS to EU keys. Snapshots can be stored in EU buckets and we can provide signed manifests for each snapshot.
- Cross-region US failover: supported. We can implement active-passive across two US pools (us-west / us-east) with automated health checks and controlled failover window.
- Delete-on-request: we expose deletion APIs and can run a backfill to remove KV/cache prefixes + inputs; target SLA 48 hours for full propagation for pinned tenants.

Options (tradeoffs)
A) Strict geo-lock (recommended for EU PHI):
  - Backups: EU-only buckets; no cross-region replication.
  - Keys: Customer-managed KMS in EU (HSM optional).
  - Recovery: manual restore to another EU region (no automatic failover).
  - Cost: higher (multi-region procurement + storage separation)

B) Warm-standby with controlled failover:
  - Backups: encrypted copies in EU, held in cold storage with encrypted manifests; failover is manual and gated by approvals.
  - Keys: KMS in EU with limited cross-region access (audit trails).
  - Cost: medium, lower RTO than strict geo-lock if you accept manual failover.

Logging and audit exports
- We can provide 12-month audit log retention by default (append-only) and a monthly export. Application logs (180 days) and security audit logs (12 months) can be partitioned by region.
- We will produce a CSV manifest for each snapshot: snapshot-id, tenant-id, region, object-manifest-hash, created-at. That can serve as the quarterly attestation artifact.

Requested next steps
1) Technical workshop (45–60 min) to map exactly which data fields (by dataset) get pinned to EU vs kept in US. I'll propose sample configuration snippets during the call.
2) Provide our recommended playbook drafts (A & B) with expected RTO/RPO and estimated delta in per-token cost.

I can run the workshop Wednesday or Thursday next week — Ben, Monica, please pick a time and I'll circulate an agenda and a brief ops checklist.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
